name: cron402-mcp

tools.name: cron402_guide
tools.description: READ THIS FIRST before using any other cron402 tool. Free, no payment. Returns the exact step-by-step procedure for scheduling a recurring webhook, what each tool costs, and the rules you must follow.

tools.name: check_wallet
tools.description: Free. Check the cron402 payment wallet before spending: returns the address, network, USDC balance, ETH balance for gas, and how many runs it can afford. Call this before create_cron or topup_cron.

tools.name: preview_schedule
tools.description: Free, no payment. Turn a schedule into a validated cron expression and show the next 5 run times in UTC. Accepts plain English like 'every 15 minutes' or 'every weekday at 9am', or a 5-field cron expression. ALWAYS call this before create_cron and show the user the result.

schedule.description: Plain English ('every 15 minutes', 'every day at 09:00', 'every monday at 5pm', 'weekly') or a 5-field cron expression ('*/15 * * * *').

timezone.description: IANA timezone of any time-of-day in the schedule, e.g. 'America/New_York'. Omit if the user gave the time in UTC.

tools.name: create_cron
tools.description: PAID: spends $0.008 USDC. Create a scheduled job that calls a webhook URL on a repeating schedule. Call this ONCE per request — calling it twice creates two jobs and charges twice. Run preview_schedule first. Returns a jobId you must report to the user. The job is created with 1 run credit, so it fires once and then stops unless you call topup_cron.

schedule.description: Plain English ('every 15 minutes', 'every weekday at 9am') or a 5-field cron expression. Validated locally before any payment is made.

url.description: Public HTTPS URL to call on every fire. localhost will never work.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for a time-of-day in the schedule, e.g. 'Europe/Berlin'.

body.description: Request body sent on every fire (POST only).

headers.description: Extra request headers, e.g. an authorization token for the target.

notifyUrl.description: Optional. Receives a POST with the result after every fire.

tools.name: topup_cron
tools.description: PAID: spends $0.008 per credit ($0.008 / $0.08 / $0.80). Add prepaid run credits to an existing job. Each credit pays for one fire. Also reactivates a job that ran out of credits. Call ONCE — repeating it charges again.

jobId.description: The job id returned by create_cron.

pack.description: How many run credits to buy: 1, 10, or 100.

tools.name: get_cron
tools.description: Free. Get one job's current status, remaining credits, next run time, and its last 20 executions with HTTP status codes and errors. Use this to answer 'is my cron working?'.

jobId.description: The job id returned by create_cron.

tools.name: list_crons
tools.description: Free. List the cron jobs created from this machine with this wallet, with each one's live status and remaining credits. Use this when the user asks what is scheduled or you have lost a job id.

tools.name: pause_cron
tools.description: Free. Stop a job from firing without deleting it. Credits are kept. Signs an EIP-712 authorization with the configured wallet — only the wallet that paid for the job can do this.

jobId.description: The job id returned by create_cron.

tools.name: resume_cron
tools.description: Free. Start a paused job firing again. The job needs at least 1 credit — if it is 'exhausted', call topup_cron instead. Signs an EIP-712 authorization with the configured wallet.

jobId.description: The job id returned by create_cron.

tools.name: delete_cron
tools.description: Free but PERMANENT and irreversible: deletes a job forever and does not refund unused credits. Confirm with the user before calling. If they only want it to stop for now, use pause_cron instead.

jobId.description: The job id returned by create_cron.
